title: 2×2 Eigenvalue Calculator
description: Compute the characteristic polynomial, eigenvalues (real or complex) and eigenvectors of any 2×2 matrix, with the full derivation shown.
howto: Enter the four entries a, b, c, d of the matrix [[a,b],[c,d]].
Press Calculate to get trace, determinant and the characteristic polynomial λ² − tr·λ + det = 0.
Read the eigenvalues — real, repeated, or complex conjugate pairs — with the quadratic-formula steps.
For real eigenvalues, the corresponding eigenvectors are shown and verified by A·v = λ·v.

faqs.q: What is the characteristic polynomial of a 2×2 matrix?
faqs.a: For [[a,b],[c,d]] it is det(A − λI) = λ² − (a+d)·λ + (ad−bc). Its roots are exactly the eigenvalues of the matrix.

faqs.q: What does a complex eigenvalue mean?
faqs.a: A complex pair α ± βi means the matrix acts as a rotation combined with scaling by √(α²+β²) — typical for rotation matrices.
For each eigenvalue λ, the tool solves (A − λI)·v = 0 by picking the row with the larger entries and setting v = (−(d−λ), c) or ((b), −(a−λ)), then verifies A·v = λ·v numerically.
